guard: an isolated worker can die without taking the custodial child PID with it, a successor can adopt the surviving seat, a childless custodian exits on its own, and a reap signals only a process whose start identity matches its record within the boot that record names
why: The fixture launches a real detached custodian, records worker and child pids, kills only the worker, then adopts the surviving seat. Both mutation windows are code-only unique anchors.

The linger cells launch real custodians whose child exits at once and watch the custodian pid; the reap cells run reapSeat against a live custodied seat and against a record whose pinned start identities do not match the live pids.

A custody reference reaches reapSeat and loadSeat from a durable slot row, so the id is checked against the shape seatId mints before it is joined to the custody root. The mutation drops that check and the traversal id resolves to a path outside the root instead of being refused.

A start token counts ticks since boot, so it is unique only within one boot while a custody record outlives a reboot on disk. The boot cells rewrite a live seat's record to name a foreign boot and then to name none, and require both to refuse rather than signal the pids that record still holds.

mutations.name: M1 suppress worker-death survival
mutations.expectRed: worker death leaves the custodial child PID running
mutations.cell: worker death leaves the custodial child PID running
mutations.note: The mutation is only the final child-live predicate after the worker is proven dead.

mutations.name: M2 re-apply hello geometry on every later
mutations.expectRed: resize: geometry survives the hello apply
mutations.cell: resize: geometry survives the hello apply
mutations.note: Unconditional hello apply is the clobber that made mesh-attach-plane miss a 90x25 resize.

mutations.name: M3 notify exit only to output subscribers
mutations.find: for (const sock of controllers) send(sock, { event: "exit" });
mutations.expectRed: onExit fires without an output subscription
mutations.cell: onExit fires without an output subscription
mutations.note: Manager readiness onExit does not subscribe to output. Output-only notify is the CI M3 process-exit miss.

mutations.name: M4 skip already-dead onExit
mutations.expectRed: onExit fires for a child that exits before hello
mutations.cell: onExit fires for a child that exits before hello
mutations.note: A child that exits before attach must still fire onExit. Manager readiness uses that path without an output subscription.

mutations.name: M5 skip subscribe output replay
mutations.find: if (early) send(sock, { event: "output", sub, data: Buffer.from(early, "utf8").toString("base64") });
mutations.expectRed: fast-exit print reaches onData before onExit
mutations.cell: fast-exit print reaches onData before onExit
mutations.note: launchSeat returns after the child pid exists, so dump-then-exit bytes are already written. Live subscribe without replay is the env-isolate empty capture.

mutations.name: M6 leave the controller socket open after waitForExit
mutations.expectRed: waitForExit drops the controller socket so the worker can exit
mutations.cell: waitForExit drops the controller socket so the worker can exit
mutations.note: A live Unix socket after waitForExit keeps the manager event loop alive through spawn-detach teardown.

mutations.name: M7 skip terminal custodian cleanup after child exit
mutations.find:
const settleTerminal = (): void => {
    if (alive || settling || !ready) return;
mutations.expectRed: natural exit: custodian process, socket, and record converge without fixture kill
mutations.cell: natural exit: custodian process, socket, and record converge without fixture kill
mutations.note: Deleting the owned terminal-settle transition leaves the Unix server, socket, record, and custodian process alive after waitForExit. The named cell must fail without fixture SIGKILL.

mutations.name: M8 treat any live pid as the recorded process
mutations.expectRed: a pid whose start identity differs from the record is treated as gone, never signalled
mutations.cell: a pid whose start identity differs from the record is treated as gone, never signalled
mutations.note: Bypassing the start-identity match is the wrong-process kill a reused pid would produce.

mutations.name: join a custody id to the root without checking its shape
mutations.expectRed: a forged custody id that walks out of the root is refused, not resolved
mutations.cell: a forged custody id that walks out of the root is refused, not resolved

mutations.name: signal a record that belongs to another boot
mutations.find:
if (boot !== undefined && rec.bootId !== boot)
    throw new Error(`seat ${id} record belongs to boot ${rec.bootId}, but this is boot ${boot}; refusing to signal pid ${rec.custodianPid}/${rec.childPid} (those pids now belong to this boot's processes)`);
mutations.expectRed: a record from another boot refuses to signal
mutations.cell: a record from another boot refuses to signal
mutations.note: Without the boot comparison the start tokens match across reboots by coincidence, and the reap signals whatever this boot put at those pid numbers.

mutations.name: write the custody record without the boot it belongs to
mutations.expectRed: the custodian stamps the boot its pids belong to
mutations.cell: the custodian stamps the boot its pids belong to
mutations.note: An unstamped record is refused by reapSeat, so every seat this custodian launches becomes unreapable rather than misreaped.

mutations.name: drop the boot stamp when a record is read back
mutations.expectRed: reapSeat signals a live seat by identity and proves it gone
mutations.cell: reapSeat signals a live seat by identity and proves it gone
mutations.note: A reader that rebuilds the record without the stamp makes every seat unreapable: the custodian writes the boot, readRecord forgets it, and reapSeat refuses the record it was handed.
